title: Serve a feed that parses as valid Atom or RSS
statement: The published feed is well-formed XML that satisfies the format it declares, so a reader that fetches it can enumerate the entries without recovering from a syntax error.
rationale: A feed with a broken element or an unclosed tag stops at the first fault in most readers, which means the entries after that point exist but reach nobody.
implementation: Generate the feed from a serializer that escapes for XML rather than from a string template, and parse the generated file during the build so a fault fails the build instead of the reader.

verification.method: Fetch the feed from the production host, parse it as XML, and confirm the required elements of the declared format are present and complete.

title: Declare the feed with an alternate link and its media type
statement: Pages the feed covers carry a link element pointing at the feed, giving the feed's media type and an absolute address, so a reader can find the feed from any page in the section.
rationale: Without that link a reader has to guess the feed's path, and a link that omits the media type gives no way to tell a feed from any other alternate representation.
implementation: Emit the link from the same configuration that generates the feed, so the declared address and the served address cannot diverge. Point section pages at their own section feed rather than at the site feed.

verification.method: Collect alternate feed links per route, fetch each declared address, and confirm the media type served matches the type the link declares.

caution: Adding a link to a feed that already exists changes no behaviour and is reversible, which is why it is permitted automatically. Creating a feed is not covered by this record.

title: Point each feed entry at its canonical page address
statement: An entry's link resolves to the canonical address of the page it describes, on the production host, without a redirect and without tracking parameters appended.
rationale: Readers and aggregators treat the entry link as the identity of the item, so a link carrying campaign parameters or pointing at a redirect propagates a non-canonical address everywhere the entry travels.
implementation: Build the entry link from the same canonical value the page emits rather than from the routing table, and drop any parameter the analytics layer would otherwise append.

verification.method: Request every entry link in the feed and compare the final address and status against the canonical value declared by the page it reaches.

title: Exclude drafts and removed items from the feed
statement: The feed contains only items currently published, and an item withdrawn after publication is dropped from the feed in the same operation that withdraws it.
rationale: A feed is fetched repeatedly and copied by whoever fetches it, so an unpublished item that appears once has been distributed before anyone notices it should not have been.
implementation: Generate the feed from the published route set rather than from a query over all records with a status filter written separately, so a new status cannot default into the feed.

verification.method: Request every item the feed lists without credentials and report any that returns a challenge, a redirect to authentication, or a removed status.

caution: This rests on the feed being a published copy of whatever it lists, which needs no citation. Removing an item from the feed does not retract copies already fetched, so an accidental publication still needs handling as a publication.

title: Keep entry identifiers stable across rebuilds
statement: Each entry carries an identifier that stays the same for the life of the item, independent of its title, its address, and its position in the feed.
rationale: Readers deduplicate on the identifier, so an identifier that changes on rebuild republishes every item as new and shows subscribers the same content again.
implementation: Derive the identifier from a persistent record key rather than from the current address or heading, and never regenerate it when the item is edited.

verification.method: Capture entry identifiers from two consecutive builds and report any identifier that changed while its item persisted.

title: Escape entry content so the feed remains well-formed
statement: Markup and reserved characters inside an entry's title or body are escaped or wrapped so the surrounding document stays parseable, whatever the item text contains.
rationale: Item text routinely contains characters that are reserved in the enclosing format, and inserting it unescaped turns a single apostrophe or ampersand in an article into a feed that fails to parse.
implementation: Let the serializer escape every text node rather than escaping selectively where a fault was once observed, and test the generator against item text containing reserved characters and embedded markup.

verification.method: Parse the served feed and additionally generate it from fixture items containing reserved characters, confirming both parse without error.
